name: 34789-docimage-paddleocrvl0.9b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one node, one GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One GPU, one engine. A 1.93 GB checkpoint fits one card many times over.
architecture: Vision-language OCR specialist: SigLIP-shaped dynamic-resolution vision tower (hidden 1152, 27 layers, image_size 384, patch 14) in front of a small bf16 decoder. Read off the HF `config.json`.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=300, bounded at 500 requests / 1800 s safety, warmup the first 10% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_image` + `synthetic_text`, single turn: one 2048x2560 JPEG page (quality 85, `content: noise`) plus a 24-token instruction per request, 790 output tokens back. Lengths are fixed (min = max = mean), and output length is forced -- the backend sets `ignore_eos` whenever `max_tokens` is set.
purpose: A document-page OCR service transcribing full-page scans into long text for 300 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# Serve flags for the engine at commit d86060122aaf68eb2387c8999f1ac94bf469c2a8
# (`v0.18.1rc0-181-gd86060122aaf6`). Nothing here is tuned.

model: PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.5
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-num-batched-tokens: 131072

# Both caches are OFF by choice, and prefix caching defaults ON at this commit.
enable-prefix-caching: false
mm-processor-cache-gb: 0

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.5
dtype: bfloat16

# The checkpoint carries an `auto_map`, so the HF processor class is loaded from the repo;
# without this flag it may refuse to load.
trust-remote-code: true

# `max-model-len` is deliberately unset: naming a context bound here could silently refuse a
# page whose visual-token count exceeds it.
